chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asadi told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Mir-Zaban told us, saying: Ali ibn Ja'd told us, saying: Shu'ba informed us, from Abu Imran al-Jouni, from Abdullah ibn Samit, who said: Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said:
I said: O Messenger of Allah, a man acts for himself and the people love him. He said: That is the hastened good news for the believer.

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, a prominent companion of the Prophet known for his asceticism and simplicity.
key_terms.عَاجِلُ بُشْرَى: Hastened good news; an early, worldly preview of the ultimate reward.
key_terms.يُحِبُّهُ النَّاسُ: The people love him; refers to public affection and social approval.

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean by 'hastened good news for the believer' when people love a man who acts for himself?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari inquires about the spiritual status of a believer whose deeds, though perhaps initially self-motivated, result in genuine public affection. The Prophet identifies this worldly approval as 'ajjal bashra' (hastened good news), a concept Shia scholars interpret as a tangible, early taste of Paradise that validates the sincerity of one's faith and serves as a precursor to the eternal reward. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the interplay between inner intention and outward social validation as signs of divine favor.
